scan-library.label: Scan entire library
scan-library.desc: Walk your root folders and index every comic file — finds files not yet in the library and drops ones deleted from disk.

reindex-series.label: Re-index series folders
reindex-series.desc: For every matched series, re-index its OWN folder and attribute the files there — authoritatively, without fuzzy matching. Fixes files that were attached to the wrong same-named series. (Finding brand-new comics is still 'Scan entire library'.)

tag-untagged.label: Tag all untagged files
tag-untagged.desc: Write metadata into every owned file that has none (converts .cbr as needed).

convert-cbr.label: Convert all CBR → CBZ
convert-cbr.desc: Repack every .cbr as a .cbz so it can be tagged and read consistently.

unwrap-nested.label: Unwrap nested archives
unwrap-nested.desc: Some releases ship a .cbz that holds a .cbr instead of pages — it opens, tags and looks healthy, and has nothing to read. This lifts the inner archive’s pages to the top level, in place, keeping the ComicInfo. Anything it cannot prove is left untouched.

redownload-corrupt.label: Re-download corrupt files
redownload-corrupt.desc: Unwrap nested archives in place, then queue a fresh download of every other corrupt comic file. Each corrupt file stays until a good copy replaces it, so an issue no source has loses nothing. Files not matched to an issue can't be fetched and are only counted.

remove-duplicates.label: Remove duplicate files
remove-duplicates.desc: Delete duplicate copies of the same issue across every comic. Corrupt copies a good one already replaced go outright. Where two GOOD copies exist, the best is kept — tagged first, then the most pages, then the largest — and the other removed; that part runs as a preview (see Logs → tools for the list) unless you tick the box.

verify.label: Verify archives
verify.desc: Deep-check every comic file for corruption and prune ones missing from disk.

relink-cv.label: Re-link files to metadata
relink-cv.desc: Re-map owned files to the metadata source's issues for every matched comic (fixes owned/missing counts).

merge-duplicate-series.label: Merge duplicate series
merge-duplicate-series.desc: Fold together series rows that point at the same volume (a copy added straight from the metadata source while the folder's own row was matched elsewhere). The folder-backed row is kept; the other's files, wanted issues and follows move over. Any duplicate copies that surface are then cleared with Remove duplicate files.

rematch-mismatched.label: Re-check mismatched volumes
rematch-mismatched.desc: Find series whose files go beyond their matched volume's last issue — the sign a same-name mini or one-shot was matched instead of the real run — and re-match them. A clear winner is applied and its files re-linked; anything unclear is left for Fix match on the series page.

refresh-series.label: Refresh series metadata
refresh-series.desc: Re-pull every matched series’ volume details and issue list from the metadata service — picks up publication status (Ongoing / Ended), enrichment for series cached before it was on, and issues published since. One request a second, so a big library takes a while; if the service rate-limits, it stops cleanly and you run it again.

fetch-metadata.label: Download issue metadata
fetch-metadata.desc: Fetch issue detail (descriptions, credits, dates, covers) for every issue in your collection that is missing it. Already-cached issues are skipped; if the metadata source rate-limits, it stops cleanly — just run it again to finish.

rename-files.label: Rename files to pattern
rename-files.desc: Rename every matched file to your file pattern (same folder — no moves) so imported scene-named files match downloaded ones. Collisions are skipped.

backup-db.label: Back up database
backup-db.desc: Snapshot the catalog database into backups/ next to it (keeps the newest 5). Safe while the app is in use. Restore: stop the app and copy a snapshot over catalog.db.

remove-ghosts.label: Remove ghost series
remove-ghosts.desc: Find leftover series from before metadata matching — no match, no files on disk — whose "wanted" issues clutter the Wanted tab but can never download. Runs as a preview (see Logs → tools for the list); tick the box to actually delete them.
